title: Write formal runbook for cutting a Runtime LTS patch release
creator: Talia Benson
description:
Convert the first-branch-cut working checklist + tribal knowledge into a formal, repeatable runbook for cutting Runtime LTS patch releases.

Why:
- Dedicated/Private customers need predictable patch cadence and auditable artifacts.
- Release weeks have been too dependent on specific people being online.
- We need a single, canonical doc to coordinate Runtime + Release Eng + SRE + Support/CS.

Scope:
- Document end-to-end steps for an LTS patch release (e.g., 1.18.1-lts): branch prep, cherry-picks/backports, CI + perf gates, artifact generation/signing/checksums, SBOM/provenance, publishing release notes, and rollout comms.
- Include clear owners per step and time estimates (wall-clock) to support planning.
- Include decision points + “stop the line” criteria (perf regression, test failures, unresolved known issues).
- Include the emergency/out-of-band security patch variant.

Out of scope:
- Changing the actual branching/versioning scheme (tracked in ENG-4822 / ADR-027).
- Building the automation itself (tracked in ENG-4823/4824/4825/4832).

Primary audience:
- Release managers (Release Eng)
- Runtime leads (kernels/scheduling)
- SRE on-call / escalation
- Private packaging engineers (installer/Helm)

Deliverable:
- Confluence runbook published under Eng → Serving Runtime → Runbooks.
- Link added to repo release-manager checklist once merged (ENG-23488 related).
acceptance_criteria:
1) Runbook published in Confluence and linked from ENG-4821 epic.
2) Runbook includes: roles/owners, prerequisites, step-by-step procedure, required gates, artifact verification steps, communication checklist, rollback guidance, and post-release follow-ups.
3) Time estimates per phase (prep / backports / gating / publish / rollout monitoring) included.
4) Reviewed by: Runtime (Noah Patel), CI/Build (Sahana Iyer), SRE (Sean Gallagher), Product (Marissa Cole), Support (Dev Patel) for correctness of the flow + handoffs.
5) Explicit “waiver/exception” process documented (perf gate flake, known issue deferral, etc.).
implementation_notes:
Proposed runbook structure (to be copied into Confluence):

A. Roles and responsibilities
- Release Manager (DRI): Connor O’Brien
- Runtime approver: Noah Patel (or delegate)
- Perf gate reviewer: Marcus Reed
- CI/build + artifact signer: Sahana Iyer
- SRE release readiness + monitoring: Sean Gallagher (Rafael Mendes as escalation)
- Release notes owner: Elliot Price
- Support/CS comms: Dev Patel / Rachel Kim

B. Inputs / prerequisites (T-7 days)
- Patch scope defined and candidate PRs labeled (lts-approved/backport-candidate/security)
- Release branch exists (runtime-1.18-lts) and is green on release-branch CI
- Perf-canary runners capacity reserved for gate window
- Signing/provenance tooling verified (keys + access)
- Known issues page reviewed; confirm no new Sev1 open regressions

C. Patch planning checklist (T-5 to T-3)
- Freeze backport intake cutoff time (except security)
- Confirm patch number, tag naming, and release note URL slug
- Create tracking doc / checklist (single source of truth) and assign owners

D. Backport execution (T-3 to T-2)
- For each PR: confirm eligibility per backport rubric
- Cherry-pick using helper script; open backport PR; require minimal diff
- Run required unit/integration tests; add/adjust targeted regression tests when appropriate
- Approvals required: Runtime owner + Release Manager; SRE required if touches scheduling/overload behavior

E. CI and deterministic build gates (T-2 to T-1)
- Release branch CI must be green (include scheduler smoke suite)
- Deterministic build check: artifact hashes consistent across reruns
- SBOM generation (or stub where applicable) attached to build artifacts

F. Performance gates (T-1)
- Required benchmark suite + GPU SKUs run
- Evaluate thresholds (p50/p95 latency, throughput) and compare to baseline
- Flake protocol: rerun once; if still noisy, escalate to Marcus + SRE for waiver decision
- Waiver format: documented rationale + affected workloads + risk assessment + approver list

G. Artifact production + verification (Release Day)
- Build/publish runtime images/binaries for LTS patch
- Generate checksums + provenance metadata; sign artifacts
- Verification: independent checksum verification by a second person
- Confirm Private installer/Helm references can pin to patch and include release notes URL

H. Release notes + documentation (Release Day)
- Generate LTS-mode release notes; curate summaries and ensure taxonomy sections present
- Update compatibility matrix (runtime ↔ CUDA/driver ↔ supported GPU SKUs ↔ installer/helm versions)
- Update known issues page with newly discovered issues and mitigations

I. Communications + rollout (Release Day + T+1)
- Internal announcements: eng-releases + support + cs + sales
- Customer-facing: Support/CS templates + Console release note link where applicable
- Rollout plan: Hosted/Dedicated staged; Private “available” notification (no forced upgrade)
- “Mandatory vs optional” criteria: define conditions (security, Sev1 crash, SLO breach)

J. Post-release monitoring + closeout (T+1 to T+3)
- Monitor LTS SLO dashboards (error rate, latency p95, crash loops)
- Confirm no new high-severity incidents; if yes, initiate backport workflow
- Retro notes: what blocked, what was manual, automation follow-ups
- Close out tracker sheet; update this runbook with deltas

K. Emergency security patch variant
- Expedited approvals, shortened intake, comms checklist, and verification steps
- Document disclosure constraints + coordinated vulnerability response process

comments: 2025-02-11 (Talia Benson): Creating this as a concrete deliverable before pilot. The branch cut thread had a lot of “do X if Y fails” that we need captured with owners/timeboxes.

2025-02-12 (Connor O'Brien): I’ll draft the runbook skeleton and pull in the branch cut checklist. Requesting reviewers: Noah (runtime), Sahana (build/signing), Sean (rollout + monitoring), Dev (support intake). Target: end of next week so we can use it for 1.18.1-lts RC.

2025-02-13 (Sahana Iyer): Please include explicit steps for: (1) verifying signing key access on release day, (2) second-person checksum verification, and (3) where SBOM artifacts are uploaded + naming convention. We’ve had failures due to missing permissions on release branches.

2025-02-14 (Sean Gallagher): Add “stop the line” criteria. If perf gate shows p95 regression above threshold OR scheduler smoke tests fail, release should hold unless we have documented waiver signed by SRE + Runtime lead. Also include a checklist for dashboards/alerts to watch during rollout.

2025-02-14 (Marissa Cole): For the comms section: make sure the runbook calls out what we need for Product/CS (release note URL, mandatory/optional flag, known issues summary). This helps with Console surfacing and enterprise comms.

2025-02-17 (Dev Patel): Add Support handoff: what we tell customers for patch availability, how to request a backport, and what diagnostics are required if they report regressions post-upgrade. We should link the support playbook once it’s final.

2025-02-20 (Connor O'Brien): Draft complete and shared for review. Added time estimates per phase and explicit rerun/waiver flow for perf flake. Incorporating feedback on artifact verification + rollout monitoring.

2025-02-24 (Noah Patel): Reviewed. Looks good. Only change requested: call out that backports touching KV cache/scheduler require adding or updating a reproducer test on the release branch (where feasible) before approval. Also clarified who can serve as runtime approver when I’m out.
2025-02-26 (Connor O'Brien): Updates applied. Published to Confluence under Serving Runtime → Runbooks. Added link to ENG-4821 epic and notified eng-releases channel. Marking Done.
